review.notes: Token-level diff of the full extracted PDF text (82 physical pages, 22,322 tokens) against the OCR markdown plus targeted verification. Code fences balanced (one txt pair at the p.17 callout); headings all numbered or standard (Change log/Contents/References); no figure-banner or speaker-label headings; 48 image embeds present. Three footnote bodies were dropped while their superscript markers survived (physical pages 6, 7, 9); each was restored after reading the rendered page. Rendered checks: p.6 (footnote 1), p.7 (footnote 2), p.9 at 300 dpi crop (footnote 3 with math). The printed 'g-mean^2' superscripts on physical p.23-25 have no footnote body anywhere in the PDF, so the OCR faithfully reproduces the source. Remaining diff hits were alignment artifacts around percent-figures and parenthesized rates that exist in the OCR text, or page furniture (page numbers, bare 'Figure N' caption labels) consistent with the source.

3 Mathematically, we plot $\log_2 R$, where $R = \frac{r_{sim}}{r_{prod}}$, against the effective positive count $k_{eff} = (\frac{1}{k_{prod}} + \frac{1}{k_{sim}})^{-1}$, with sampling-noise bounds $\pm\frac{1.645}{\ln 2}$ because $Var(\log_2 R) \approx \frac{1}{(\ln 2)^2 k_{eff}}$. Falling outside these bounds corresponds to rejecting $H_0 : r_{sim} = r_{prod}$ using an approximate two-sided Wald test at the 10% significance level. The plotted confidence region does not leverage the paired nature of samples and resamples, which may lead it to be overly wide. Intervals based on paired-samples did not seem to meaningfully change the borders while introducing additional mathematical complexity.
